unable: not having the skill, means, or opportunity to do something
Diseases such as polio once left many children unable to walk.
walk: an act of travelling on foot
A community could travel further than a day's walk from home when needed.
disappeared: stopped being visible or ceased to exist
The hiker disappeared into the fog and was not seen again.
region: an area of a country or the world with particular features
The mountainous region attracts hikers from all over the world.
success: the achievement of a desired aim or result
Her hard work eventually led to great success in business.
create: cause something new to exist; bring into being
The chef wanted to create a dish that combined two very different cuisines.
strange: unusual or surprising; difficult to understand
There was something strange about the silence in the house.
problem: a matter that is difficult to deal with or solve
The main problem with the plan was its enormous cost.
no: not any; used to indicate a complete absence
There was no sound at all in the empty hall.
longer: for a greater length of time
Fresh bread stays soft for longer if wrapped properly.
see: to perceive something with the eyes
From the hilltop you can see the whole valley below.
becomes: The sky becomes darker earlier as autumn approaches.
easier: The new software makes editing photos much easier.
believe: to accept that something is true
Most scientists believe the data supports a gradual rather than sudden change.
unnecessary: not needed; more than is required
Sometimes replanting is unnecessary: clear the ground, wait, and the old community returns.
doubts: She had serious doubts about accepting the new job offer.
about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
tend: to be likely to do or be something, usually
Older houses in this area tend to have thicker walls.
grow: produce or cultivate a plant or crop
Many families grow vegetables in small plots behind their houses.
become: It can take years of practice to become a skilled musician.
false: The witness gave a false statement to the police.
stories: accounts of events, real or imagined, told for interest
Grandmother told us stories about life before the war.
spread: to extend over a larger area or reach more people over time
The fire spread quickly through the dry forest.
quickly: The fire spread quickly through the dry grass before anyone noticed.
online: connected to or available through the internet
More people now shop online instead of visiting physical stores.
while: It makes the city liveable while the wider problem is dealt with separately.
invisible: Radio waves are invisible but carry signals across long distances.
girl: a female child or young woman
The girl practised the piano for an hour every day.
caught: captured, seized, or stopped partway through an action
bị bắt, bị chặn giữa chừng
The thief was caught trying to climb over the fence.
learned: gained knowledge or skill through study or experience
She learned to cook traditional dishes from her grandmother.
lesson: a period of teaching, or something learned from experience
The teacher planned an interactive lesson about the water cycle.
hard: difficult; not easy, or solid to the touch
It was hard to concentrate with all that noise outside.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
suffering: the experience of pain, distress or hardship
The charity works to reduce suffering caused by famine.
any: used to refer to one or some of a thing, no matter which
Do you have any questions before we begin the meeting?
though: She smiled, though she was clearly exhausted from the trip.
protects: keeps someone or something safe from harm
A strong immune system protects the body against many common infections.
community: a group of people living in the same place or sharing something
The whole community gathered to celebrate the festival in the town square.
